 Sponsored Content:
 Justin Reid’s tenure with his home-state team has appeared to reach an end.
 According to a r eport from NFL Insider Jordan Schultz , the New Orleans Saints are planning to grant Reid’s request for the team to release him.
 Head coach Kellen Moore does not speak with the media on Thursdays, but defensive coordinator Brandon Staley said the team is “working through some things with that matter” and that it will “come to a resolution shortly.” Staley added that he was surprised by the turn of events.
 New Orleans signed Reid to a three-year, $31.5 million contract prior to the start of last season, bringing the Louisiana native in as a veteran presence with a championship pedigree to help turn around the fortunes of a team that had not reached the playoffs since the 2020 season.
 Reid’s teammates also voted him a team captain prior to the start of the season. This is the second straight season a team captain requested their release midway through the season, with Brandin Cooks being granted his release after 10 games in 2025.
 “The football business side of things is different from the culture of the locker room,” Staley said. “Speaking of our defensive culture, it’s been strong for two years. We have a really close group.”
 But Reid’s play declined this season, especially of late, when he had several notable missed tackles toward the ends of both the Cleveland and Carolina games that led to big plays.
 New Orleans had started to cut into Reid’s playing time by using Jordan Howden in his place on the field, playing 77 and 79 % of the snaps the last two weeks, respectively. Staley said he doesn’t recall any conversations between himself and Reid about taking away his starting role moving forward.
 Staley said he expects to turn full-time to Howden at safety rather than rotating Jonas Sanker back to the position he played a year ago.
 “I know that I’ve really enjoyed working with him,” Staley said. “There are some things that we all want a little bit more of from a productivity standpoint, but in terms of the fit, in terms of how he’s been here, he’s been a pleasure to coach. I’ll just leave it at that.”
 In 24 games with the Saints, Reid recorded 118 tackles and one interception. He had yet to break up a pass in nine starts this season.
 “I’m very excited about him,” Staley said of Howden. “I thought last year he played at a real starting level in the snaps that he played and in some of the games he started last year for us. We have a lot of confidence in him. '
 “… He looks like a pro safety when he’s played for us. The increased snaps for him this year have been a real credit for him, because he’s earned them. He’s playing the right way, he played a good game against Carolina, and we’ve got to stay with him because he’s still improving, there’s still so much in front of him.”
